transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Since the ice returned so quickly after a manual defrost, it suggests your automatic defrost system has stopped working. This is usually caused by either a faulty heater/thermostat (which stops melting the frost automatically) or a blocked drain hole at the bottom of the freezer back wall. To narrow this down and find the correct replacement part if needed, I need the model number. It’s typically on a sticker inside the fridge or freezer compartment—often near the salad drawer or on the side wall.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W (indesit), read it off the rating plate. its a static freezer tho, manual defrost, no auto defrost

Thanks for clarifying—it’s a static model, so there isn’t an automatic defrost system. Since the ice returned in just two weeks, the most likely cause is either a blocked drain hole at the bottom of the back wall (where meltwater should run away) or warm air getting in through a worn door seal. To narrow this down: with the freezer empty and fully defrosted, look at the back wall inside. Is there a small drain hole or channel at the bottom? If so, is it clear (you can see through it) or blocked with ice/debris?
not sure about a drain hole, static freezer so not sure it has one. i can see the bottom corner of the door seal is split tho, about 5cm

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That 5cm split in the bottom corner of the door seal is probably why your freezer is icing up again. To fix this, you will need to replace the door seal (gasket). Since I cannot confirm the exact gasket type for your specific Indesit IB55532W model number in my database, please contact Indesit customer support or a reputable appliance parts supplier with that model number to get the correct part. Once you have it, replacing a seal is usually a straightforward owner-safe job: you pull out the old rubber seal from its groove and press the new one in (sometimes starting at the hinge corners). Make sure the door closes firmly all around once it's fitted.
